findings.bug: launcher_records matches only PID. The initial capture and exercise feed it the entire retained same-boot log. Stable current /proc starttime checks do not bind old log lines to that current process instance. If a PID is reused and the current instance's startup records are absent, the previous instance's ready/patch/power records satisfy startup attribution and capture returns PASS.
findings.fix: Require initial session/startup records to be inside a verifiable current-process birth window, using compatible device clock bases and actual CLK_TCK. If this cannot be established, preserve INCONCLUSIVE or use explicitly requested establish-session. Do not reconstruct old log time from the present wall clock across possible wall-clock changes.
findings.reproduced: The unmodified Probe.run/capture and record parsers accept old PID 410/session 12 logs even though the current stable PID 410 has later starttime 20000 and its session 13 records are absent. Actual result is exit 0/PASS, expected INCONCLUSIVE.
findings.title: Bind initial startup records to the current process birth, not only its PID

limitations: All fixtures are synthetic or mocked host verification; no ADB was executed and no handset outcome is claimed.
This review covers the probe, not a new audit of the launcher/broker production implementation.
The initial f24e5657 snapshot is frozen. A later author revision must be reviewed separately; this report must not be relabeled PASS.

reviewed_controls.details: Exactly 30 unique safe paths, raw readback hashes and row kinds, receipt, build incremental, boot ID, clean pinned build inputs, factory-launcher rejection, loaded wmt_drv, live executable/module hashes, exact argv and one /dev/stpwmt fd are checked. Future build19 input values and handset state were not audited here.

reviewed_controls.area: Live process identity and SIGTERM targeting
reviewed_controls.details: Snapshot surrounds proc inspection with starttime checks; worker polling rejects reuse; the signal command checks positive integer PID/starttime, executable path and non-factory hash before SIGTERM. Device-wide SIGKILL/ctl.stop are absent.

Three stable TID sets, one additional worker, main-thread-only baseline, old-process disappearance, new PID/newer birth, source-ready/session advancement, power completion and Wi-Fi traffic checks are explicit. Controlled-restart log prefix and source-bound old-main-TID kernel mode window are separate from initial startup attribution affected by RTP-1.
Missing records/source binding produce INCONCLUSIVE and propagate to the top level. This is attribution of existing mode write/read logs, not independent final register state.

Mutation is marked before commands; original property is captured beforehand and restored exactly including empty. Cleanup attempts source-service recovery, preserves the primary failure, and cleanup failure forces FAIL. Host reader shutdown never signals the device launcher.

scope: Bounded read-only review of the seven frozen wmt-source-launcher-probe files; no production, build-project, or handset changes
